subject: Horizon Health: compact security architecture packet for SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 13:05 -0700
Subject: Quick request — compact network + isolation summary for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing our SIG/CAIQ submission and the scorer asked for a short, focused security architecture packet that shows the network boundaries and isolation model for the Dedicated and Private deployment options you offer. Specifically they're asking for: a single-page topology diagram (control plane vs data plane), a one-paragraph narrative describing tenant/egress controls, and a short mapping to the CAIQ/SIG sections for network isolation and key management.

Can you send a concise packet (diagram + ~1 page narrative + an evidence map) by EOD Thursday our time? We have a SIG deadline next week and want to include a Redwood snapshot. If you have a small exec-friendly diagram as well, that helps for our compliance committee.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Director, Cloud Engineering
Horizon Health

P.S. cc'ing security@horizonhealth.com for visibility.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 14:02 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick request — compact network + isolation summary for SIG/CAIQ

Ben / Kimberly — forwarding Sara's request from Horizon. They want a compact packet for SIG/CAIQ that covers Dedicated and Private. Target: single-page topology diagram (control/data plane split), 1-page narrative, and an evidence map (spreadsheet mapping CAIQ/SIG questions to our artifacts or excerpts). Horizon prefers an exec-friendly one-slide summary + a technical appendix.

Priorities / ask:
- Ben: can you draft the topology diagram(s) and a short legends file (SVG preferred) — show control plane isolation, tenant fencing, egress policing, and the KMS/HSM boundary.
- Kimberly: please draft the narrative and the CAIQ mapping table rows. Highlight any items that will need customer-side attestations (e.g., VPC peering config, last-mile VPN).

Deadlines: internal draft by EOD tomorrow so I can QC and send to Sara Thursday morning their time.

Please attach all working files to the thread. I will handle final packaging and delivery.

Marissa
Account Exec, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23 09:16 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick request — compact network + isolation summary for SIG/CAIQ

Marissa / Kim — initial draft attached. Files included in this send: Horizon-arch-draft.pdf (4 pages: 1-page executive diagram, 2-page technical diagram with numbered zones, 1-page appendix), network-legend.svg, and evidence-map.xlsx (stub rows for network/keys/egress).

Quick notes on open items I called out in the spreadsheet:
- KMS/HSM: we document customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys in the Private deployment; need a short snippet from infra about key rotation and access controls (I flagged for infra).
- Egress justification: we included default NAT egress + optional NAT-less peering; need a sentence confirming how we log and fingerprint egress flows for audit (NetFlow/flow logs).
- Last-mile: Horizon will need to confirm whether they want VPC peering or Site-to-Site VPN for Dedicated; that affects routing tables we show in the diagram.

Attachments: Horizon-arch-draft.pdf (application/pdf), network-legend.svg (image/svg+xml), evidence-map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23 11:48 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick request — compact network + isolation summary for SIG/CAIQ

Thanks Ben — that looks good. A few quick edits / asks before we send to Horizon:

1) Executive slide: please reduce the diagram to the essentials (control plane, data plane, tenant fence, egress arrow). I'll craft a one-paragraph blurb that reads well for auditors.
2) Can we add a short callout about fallbacks: model variant routing and automatic fallback to an approved hosted variant if Dedicated capacity is unavailable? Horizon's auditors like to see graceful degradation.
3) In the evidence map, add a row referencing our SOC 2 control for network segregation (SOC-SEC-03) and map it to the topology figure + console logs example.

Attached a compact executive brief (horizon-exec-brief.pdf) with my draft blurb and a suggested ordering of artifacts. If Ben can incorporate the blurb and add the SOC-2 mapping row, I'm happy to finalize the packet.

Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: horizon-exec-brief.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, psc@thirdpartysec.com
Date: 2028-03-24 09:42 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick request — compact network + isolation summary for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Sara — thanks for the ask and for the patience. Attached is our consolidated security architecture packet for Horizon (redwood-horizon-security-packet-v1.1.zip). Contents (high level):

- Executive snapshot: 1-page topology diagram showing control plane vs data plane, tenant fencing, and egress flows (PDF).
- Technical appendix: detailed zone diagram for Dedicated and Private with numbering for CAIQ references (PDF).
- Evidence map: spreadsheet mapping CAIQ/SIG questions to specific artifacts and excerpts (XLSX).
- Legends & diagrams: SVG legend and a reduced diagram for executive reviewers.
- Short narrative: one-page description of how tenant isolation is enforced, KMS/HSM boundaries, and logging/egress controls.

Callouts:
- KMS: Private deployments support customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS; we've included a short excerpt describing key rotation and access gating.
- Egress & logging: we log flow-level metadata and surface flow logs via the Console; evidence map points to sample logs and retention policy.
- Graceful degradation: documented fallback to verified hosted model variants to preserve availability; noted in the narrative and evidence map.

Next steps: could we schedule a 45–60 minute walkthrough with your security team and psc@thirdpartysec.com so we can walk the packet and answer any follow-ups? I can be flexible on Thursday or Friday afternoon PT.

Links & artifacts: HubSpot HS-0048123 (deal record) and the Drive link in the related_links field above. If you want a redacted packet for external distribution, I can produce a redacted PDF.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-horizon-security-packet-v1.1.zip (contains the files listed above)
